'''The Hyperborean Maidens of Delos: Myth and Offerings''' tells the Greek tradition of the young women who came from the Hyperboreans — the people "beyond the North Wind" — to the sacred island of Delos, died there, and were honoured at their tombs for centuries; and it sets beside it what archaeology found on Delos. Alpha.

== 1. The tradition in Herodotus ==

Herodotus (''Histories'' 4.32–35), writing in the 5th century BCE and citing the Delians themselves, gives the fullest account:

* '''Two pairs of maidens.''' First came '''Arge and Opis''', who arrived with the goddesses Apollo and Artemis themselves, bringing thank-offerings to Eileithyia for an easy childbirth. Later came '''Hyperoche and Laodice''', escorted by five men the Delians called ''Perpherees'' ("bearers"), bringing offerings to Delos.
* '''They never went home.''' The second pair died on Delos. Their tomb (''sēma'') lay inside the sanctuary of Artemis, to the left of the entrance, with an olive tree growing on it.
* '''The hair offering.''' Delian girls before marriage cut a lock of hair, wound it round a spindle and laid it on the maidens' tomb; Delian boys wound theirs round a green shoot and laid it there too.
* '''The offerings' route.''' Offerings "wrapped in wheat straw" were passed from people to people — through the Scythians, westward to the Adriatic, south to Dodona, then the Malian Gulf, Euboea, Karystos, Tenos — and so to Delos. The Hyperboreans sent them this way after their own escort failed to return.
* Arge and Opis had their own honours: hymns composed by '''Olen''' of Lycia, and ashes from sacrifices scattered on their tomb behind the Artemision.

== 2. Other versions ==

* '''Callimachus''' (''Hymn to Delos'', 3rd century BCE) names the maidens '''Oupis, Loxo and Hekaerge''', daughters of Boreas, the North Wind.
* '''Pausanias''' (1.31.2) gives a different route for the straw-wrapped offerings, through the Arimaspians, Issedones and Scythians to Sinope, then through Greece to Prasiae in Attica and Delos.
* Hekaerge and Opis also appear as by-names of Artemis herself — the maidens may be the goddess's own attendants or doubles.

== 3. Archaeology on Delos ==

* '''Record:''' French excavators found, near the Artemision, a Bronze Age (Mycenaean) tomb enclosure that has been identified with the tomb of Hyperoche and Laodice (the ''Sēma''), and another structure identified with the ''Thēkē'' of Arge and Opis. The identifications are widely accepted but rest on matching Herodotus's description to the ground.
* '''Record:''' The tombs were far older than the classical sanctuary — the Delians of Herodotus's day were honouring a Bronze Age grave as the burial of the northern maidens.

== 4. Readings and debate ==

* '''Debated:''' Many scholars read the "Hyperborean" offering route as a memory of real long-distance exchange — the prehistoric amber routes from the Baltic and North Sea to the Mediterranean. Baltic amber is found in Mycenaean graves.
* '''Debated:''' Who the Hyperboreans "were" has been argued for 2,500 years — the far north of Europe, the steppe, Britain (Diodorus 2.47 describes an island in the northern ocean with a round temple of Apollo, often linked to Stonehenge), or a purely mythical paradise.
* '''Tradition:''' Apollo was said to spend the winter months among the Hyperboreans, returning to Delphi in spring.
* '''Hypothesis:''' the operator links the maidens to an ancient temple lineage whose women travelled between sanctuaries; see [[The Temple Lineage Hypothesis (Van Kush Ancestry)]].
